rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has wa-awṣā, found in the codices of the Hijaz and Syria.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( واوصى ) وهي في مصاحف اهل الحجاز والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in bihā refers to Abraham’s ‘I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds,’ construed as a word or sentence.
rows.anchor: والضمير في ﴿ بها ﴾ لقوله ﴿ أسلمت لرب العالمين ﴾ على تأويل الكلمة والجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun is supported by calling the statement a lasting word in the parallel Abraham passage.
rows.anchor: ونحوه رجوع الضمير في قوله ﴿ وجعلها كلمة باقية ﴾ الزخرف 28

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With Yaʿqūb nominative, he is coordinated with Abraham and shares the ruling: Jacob also enjoined his sons.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويعقوب ﴾ الزخرف 26 - 27 عطف على إبراهيم داخل في حكمه والمعنى ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accusative reading of Yaʿqūb coordinates him with the sons: Abraham enjoined his sons and grandson.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ويعقوب ) بالنصب عطفا على بنيه ومعناه ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ونافلته يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative yā-bunayya is governed by an implied ‘he said’ for Basrans; Kufans attach it to waṣṣā because that verb means ‘said.’
rows.anchor: على إضمار القول عند البصريين وعند الكوفيين يتعلق بوصى لأنه في معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū and Ibn Masʿūd read the vocative with an explicit an.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي وابن مسعود ( أن يا بني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Islam for Abraham’s descendants as the best religion and enabled them to follow it.
rows.anchor: أعطاكم الدين الذي هو صفوة الأديان وهو دين الاسلام ووفقكم للأخذ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is really against dying in a state other than Islam; it does not prohibit death itself, and marks death outside steadfast Islam as devoid of good.
rows.anchor: فلا يكن موتكم الا على حال كونكم ثابتين على الإسلام فالنهي في الحقيقة عن كونهم على خلاف حال الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same wording can forbid prayer without humility: formally it addresses prayer to emphasize that prayer without humility is no prayer.
rows.anchor: لا تصل الا وانت خاشع فلا تنهاه عن الصلاة ولكن عن ترك الخشوع في حال صلاته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying says that a neighbor of the mosque has no prayer except in the mosque, illustrating the construction.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 57 ( لا صلاة لجار المسجد الا في المسجد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, ‘die as a martyr’ means be in the state of martyrs when death comes, acknowledging that death’s honor.
rows.anchor: وتقول في الأمر أيضا مت وانت شهيد وليس مرادك الأمر بالموت ولكن بالكون على صفة الشهداء اذا مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is disconnected and rebuking; shahīd means present, and believers did not witness Jacob’s death but know it by revelation.
rows.anchor: الشهداء جمع شهيد ، بمعنى الحاضر : أي ما كنتم حاضرين يعقوب عليه السلام إذ حضره الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view addresses Jews, who claimed prophets died as Jews; witnessing Jacob’s demand for Islam would have exposed that claim.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب لليهود ، لأنهم كانوا يقولون : ما مات نبي إلا على اليهودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the disconnected reading fits Jews poorly, he prefers a connected question with an implied charge: were they alleging prophets were Jews? Their ancestors witnessed Jacob demand monotheism.
rows.anchor: ولكن الوجه ان تكون متصلة على ان يقدر قبلها محذوف كانه قيل أتدعون على الأنبياء اليهودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dialect pronounces ḥaḍara with kasra on the ḍād.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( حضر ) بكسر الضاد وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is general, unlike man, which scholars use for rational beings; ‘whom do you worship?’ would exclude other objects of worship.
rows.anchor: عام في كل شيء فإذا علم فرق بما ومن وكفاك دليلا قول العلماء ( من ) لما يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā taʿbudūn can ask about the worshipped being’s attributes, as ‘What is Zayd?’ asks whether he is a jurist or physician.
rows.anchor: سؤال عن صفة المعبود كما تقول ما زيد تريد أفقيه أم طبيب أم غير ذلك من الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac explain ‘your fathers’; Ishmael’s inclusion, though he was Jacob’s uncle, is known through revelation.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان لآبائك وجعل إسماعيل وهو عمه من طريق الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He again favors an implied accusation and connected am when Jews are addressed.
rows.anchor: فالآية منافية لقولهم فكيف يقال لهم ( أم كنتم شهداء ) ولكن الوجه ان تكون أم متصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā asks generally what is worshipped, unlike man, restricted to rational beings; it can also ask about the object’s quality.
rows.anchor: عام في كل شيء فإذا علم فرق بما ومن وكفاك دليلا قول العلماء ( من ) لما يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael, Jacob’s uncle, is counted among his forefathers because an uncle is like a father and an aunt like a mother, as siblings have equal standing.
rows.anchor: وجعل إسماعيل وهو عمه من جملة آبائه لأن العم أب والخالة أم لانخراطهما في سلك واحد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares a paternal uncle to a father’s peer.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه السلام 58 ( عم الرجل صنو أبيه )

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: A saying about al-ʿAbbās calls him the remnant of the Prophet’s forefathers.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام في العباس 59 ( هذا بقية آبايك

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: The Prophet asks to bring his father, fearing Quraysh may treat him as Thaqīf treated ʿUrwa b. Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: 60 ( ردوا علي أبي فإني أخشى ان تفعل به قريش ما فعلت ثقيف بعروة بن مسعود )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy reads ‘and the god of Abraham,’ omitting ‘your fathers’; abīka may be singular with Abraham as apposition or a plural form.
rows.anchor: بطرح آبائك وقرىء ( أبيك ) وفيه وجهان ان يكون واحدا وإبراهيم وحده عطف بيان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An otherwise unnamed poetic line attests al-abīnā as a plural of father.
rows.anchor: وان يكون جمعا بالواو والنون قال ( وفديننا بالأبينا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilāhan wāḥidan is an appositional substitute for ‘the god of your fathers,’ like the Quranic construction ‘by the forelock, a lying forelock.’
rows.anchor: أو على الاختصاص أي نريد بإلاه آبائك الها واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it is specification: ‘we mean one god by the god of your fathers.’
rows.anchor: أو على الاختصاص أي نريد بإلاه آبائك الها واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We submit to Him’ may be a circumstantial clause attached to subject or object of ‘worship’; it may also coordinate or parenthetically affirm sincere monotheism and submission.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل نعبد أو من مفعوله لرجوع الهاء اليه في له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Goliath was a giant Amalekite descended from ʿAmliq son of ʿĀd; his helmet weighed three hundred ratls.
rows.anchor: جبار من العمالقة من اولاد عمليق بن عاد وكانت بيضته فيها ثلثمائة رطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking God to steady their feet means granting battlefield resilience through courage, striking fear into the enemy, and similar means.
rows.anchor: وهب لنا ما نثبت به في مداحض الحرب من قوة القلوب والقاء الرعب في قلب العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David, Jesse’s youngest son and a shepherd, was the seventh son in Talut’s army; revelation told Samuel he would kill Goliath, and David slew him with three stones that called to him.
rows.anchor: كان ايشى أبو داود في عسكر طالوت مع ستة من بنيه وكان داود سابعهم وهو صغير يرعى الغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talut married his daughter to David after David killed Goliath.
rows.anchor: ورمى بها جالوت فقتله وزوجه طالوت بنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Talut envied David and sought to kill him, then repented.
rows.anchor: وروي انه حسده واراد قتله ثم تاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted David kingship across the eastern and western reaches of the Holy Land; Israel had never united under one king before David.
rows.anchor: في مشارق الأرض المقدسة ومغاربها وما اجتمعت بنو إسرائيل على ملك قط قبل داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom here means prophethood.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والحكمة ﴾ والنبوة ﴿ وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught David armor-making, the speech of birds and animals, and other knowledge.
rows.anchor: من صنعة الدروع وكلام الطير والدواب وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God making some people repel others, corrupters would dominate and earth’s benefits, agriculture, and reproduction would fail.
rows.anchor: لغلب المفسدون وفسدت الأرض وبطلت منافعها وتعطلت مصالحها من الحرث والنسل

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God’s aid to Muslims against disbelievers prevents their devastation and killing of Muslims; absent mutual restraint, disbelief and divine wrath would destroy inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقيل ولولا ان الله ينصر المسلمين على الكفار لفسدت الأرض بعيث الكفار فيها وقتل المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadāyantum means dealing with one another in debt; Ruʾba’s line illustrates the verb dāyantu.
rows.anchor: إذا داين بعضكم بعضا يقال داينت الرجل اذا عاملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debt may be owed by or to the person, as bāyaʿtuhu can mean selling to or buying from him.
rows.anchor: معطيا أو آخذا كما تقول بايعته اذا بعته أو باعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning debt supplies the antecedent for ‘write it,’ improves the wording, and distinguishes deferred from immediate debt.
rows.anchor: ذكر ليرجع الضمير إليه في قوله ﴿ فاكتبوه ﴾ إذ لو لم يذكر لوجب أن يقال فاكتبوا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A specified term must be known; harvest, threshing, or pilgrims’ return is too indeterminate.
rows.anchor: من حق الأجل ان يكون معلوما كالتوقيت بالسنة والأشهر والأيام ولو قال إلى الحصاد أو الدياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is recommended because it gives stronger security against forgetting and denial.
rows.anchor: وإنما امر بكتبة الدين لأن ذلك اوثق وآمن من النسيان وأبعد من الجحود والأمر للندب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse concerns salam: after usury was forbidden, advance sale for a guaranteed term was permitted and the longest verse revealed for it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المراد به السلم وقال لما حرم الله الربا أباح السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘With justice’ describes a trustworthy scribe who writes evenly and carefully, adding and omitting nothing; parties should choose a learned jurist who knows legal conditions.
rows.anchor: متعلق بكاتب صفة له أي كاتب مامون على ما يكتب يكتب بالسوية والاحتياط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ‘a scribe’ generalizes the prohibition: no scribe should refuse to write.
rows.anchor: ولا يمتنع أحد من الكتاب وهو معنى تنكير كاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘As God taught him’ means to write documents without altering them.
rows.anchor: مثل ما علمه الله كتابة الوثائق لا يبدل ولا يغير

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, as in 28:77, the writer should benefit others through the skill God taught him.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو كقوله تعالى ﴿ وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ﴾ القصص 77

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī regards writing as a communal obligation.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي هي فرض كفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘As God taught him’ may attach to ‘write’ in the prohibition or to the later command, producing different scopes.
rows.anchor: كما علمه الله يجوز ان يتعلق بان يكتب وبقوله فليكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase attaches to ‘write,’ the scribe must use that taught form; if it attaches to ‘let him write,’ refusal is prohibited generally before writing is ordered with qualifications.
rows.anchor: يعني فليكتب تلك الكتابة لا يعدل عنها للتوكيد وإن علقته بقوله فليكتب فقد نهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor alone dictates because the debt is witnessed against him as fixed in his liability and acknowledged by him.
rows.anchor: ولا يكن المملي الا من وجب عليه الحق لأنه هو المشهود على ثباته في ذمته وإقراره به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imlāʾ and imlāl are two Arabic forms, both used in the Quran.
rows.anchor: والإملاء والإملال لغتان قد نطق بهما القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakhsa means a reduction from a debt or right.
rows.anchor: من الحق ﴿ شيئا ﴾ والبخس النقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings omit the hamza in shayan or pronounce it with gemination.
rows.anchor: والبخس النقص وقرىء ( شيا ) بطرح الهمزة ( وشيا ) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A safīh is restricted for wastefulness and poor judgment; a weak person may be a child or confused elder, and inability to dictate may come from speech difficulty or muteness.
rows.anchor: محجورا عليه لتبذيره وجهله بالتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian dictates for a restricted or minor person, an agent for someone unable, or an interpreter for a person who confirms his translation.
rows.anchor: الذي يلي أمره من وصي إن كان سفيها أو صبيا أو وكيل إن كان غير مستطيع أو ترجمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He himself cannot dictate’ means he can dictate through another who interprets for him.
rows.anchor: فيه انه غير مستطيع بنفسه ولكن بغيره وهو الذي يترجم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek two male witnesses from believing men; most scholars require witnesses to be Muslim, free, and adult.
rows.anchor: من رجال المؤمنين والحرية والبلوغ شرط مع الاسلام عند عامة العلماء

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī rules that an enslaved person’s testimony is invalid in any matter.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه لا تجوز شهادة العبد في شيء

rows.speaker: شريح وابن سيرين وعثمان البتي
rows.claim: Shurayḥ, Ibn Sīrīn, and ʿUthmān al-Battī allow testimony by enslaved people.
rows.anchor: وعند شريح وابن سيرين وعثمان البتي انها جائزة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits non-Muslims to testify within their own religious communities.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عند أبي حنيفة شهادة الكفار بعضهم على بعض على اختلاف الملل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness; Abū Ḥanīfa accepts women’s testimony with men except in ḥudūd and retaliation.
rows.anchor: فليشهد رجل وامرأتان وشهادة النساء مع الرجال مقبولة عند أبي حنيفة فيما عدا الحدود والقصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acceptable witnesses are those whose uprightness is known.
rows.anchor: ممن تعرفون عدالتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Lest one err’ means fail to recall the testimony; purpose is phrased by its cause and effect, like preparing a prop for a leaning wall or a weapon for an approaching enemy.
rows.anchor: أن لا تهتدي احداهما للشهادة بان تنساها من ضل الطريق اذا لم يهتد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cause-effect construction works because the two are closely linked; intent to remind is expressed as intent that one err.
rows.anchor: كانت ارادة الضلال المسبب عنه الإذكار إرادة للإذكار فكانه قيل إرادة ان تذكر احداهما الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings have fatadhakkara light or doubled, fatadhākarā, and Hamza’s conditional in tidilla with indicative fatadhakkaru.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( فتذكر ) بالتخفيف والتشديد وهما لغتان و ( فتذاكرا ) وقرأ حمزة ( إن تضل احداهما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive feminine reading of ‘if one errs’ is reported; the gloss that two women together become one man is a bizarre interpretation.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه ﴾ المائدة 95 وقرىء ( ان تضل احداهما ) على البناء للمفعول والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation that the two women together count as a male is a bizarre gloss.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير فتذكر فتجعل احداهما الأخرى ذكرا يعني انهما اذا اجتمعتا كانتا بمنزلة الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses must not refuse when summoned to give testimony.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذا ما دعوا ﴾ ليقيموا الشهادة

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they are summoned to bear testimony; they may be called witnesses before bearing it because the imminent is named as present.
rows.anchor: وقيل ليستشهدوا وقيل لهم شهداء قبل التحمل تنزيلا لما يشارف منزلة الكائن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says a verse was revealed after a man visited a large gathering and nobody followed him, illustrating refusal to respond.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة كان الرجل يطوف في الحواء العظيم فيه القوم فلا يتبعه منهم أحد فنزلت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying says a believer does not say ‘I am lazy’; weariness can mean laziness, a hypocrite’s trait.
rows.anchor: كني بالسأم عن الكسل لأن الكسل صفة المنافق ومنه الحديث 153 ( لا يقول المؤمن كسلت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequent debtors may tire of preparing a separate document for each small or large debt.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد من كثرت مدايناته فاحتاج ان يكسب لكل دين صغير أو كبير كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Write it’ can refer to the debt or right; small or large describes the debt, or the document’s concise or full length without omission.
rows.anchor: والضمير في ﴿ تكتبوه ﴾ للدين أو الحق ﴿ صغيرا أو كبيرا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agreed term is the time the parties named; dhālikum points to writing as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إلى أجله ﴾ إلى وقته الذي اتفق الغريمان على تسميته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqsaṭ means more just, aqwam more supportive of testimony, and the directions make doubt less likely.
rows.anchor: أعدل من القسط ﴿ وأقوم للشهادة ﴾ وأعون على إقامة الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Sībawayh, aqsaṭ and aqwam may derive regularly from verbs or by analogy from qāsiṭ and qayyim, meaning possessed of justice and uprightness.
rows.anchor: يجوز على مذهب سيبويه ان يكونا مبنيين من أقسط وأقام وان يكون أقسط من قاسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has yāʾ for both occurrences of ‘they grow weary.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ولا يسأموا ان يكتبوه ) بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present trade means exchanged goods and hand-to-hand exchange; an immediate sale need not be written because deferred-debt risks do not arise.
rows.anchor: اريد بالتجارة ما يتجر فيه من الابدال ومعنى إدارتها بينهم تعاطيهم إياها يدا بيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade is read nominative with kāna complete or incomplete, or accusative in an excepted construction illustrated by poetry.
rows.anchor: وقرىء تجارة حاضرة بالرفع على كان التامة وقيل هي الناقصة على ان الاسم ( تجارة حاضرة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witness any sale, immediate or deferred, as a precaution against disputes; alternatively, witnessing alone can suffice for immediate trade without writing.
rows.anchor: امر بالإشهاد على التبايع مطلقا ناجزا أو كالئا لأنه احوط وأبعد مما عسى يقع من الاختلاف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says one may choose whether to witness a sale.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ان شاء أشهد وإن شاء لم يشهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk considers witnessing obligatory even for a bunch of greens.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك هي عزيمة من الله ولو على باقة بقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍārr may be active or passive; ʿUmar’s and Ibn ʿAbbās’s readings clarify it. The ban covers refusing, falsifying, adding, or omitting testimony, or harming witnesses through coercion, unpaid work, and travel costs.
rows.anchor: يحتمل البناء للفاعل والمفعول والدليل عليه قراءة عمر رضي الله عنه ( ولا يضارر ) بالإظهار والكسر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( ولا يضار ) بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘If you do so’ means if you harm one another; alternatively, it means doing anything forbidden in the passage.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإن تفعلوا ﴾ وإن تضاروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a journey means while travelling.
rows.anchor: ﴿ على سفر ﴾ مسافرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ubayy read kitāban; Ibn ʿAbbās asks what if a scribe is found but paper and ink are not.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبي رضي الله عنهما ( كتابا ) وقال ابن عباس أرأيت إن وجدت الكاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya reads kutuban; al-Ḥasan’s kitāban is glossed as the plural of kātib.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية ( كتبا ) وقرأ الحسن ( كتابا ) جمع كاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pledge is a security; variants include ruhan and rihān, with different vowels and number.
rows.anchor: فالذي يستوثق به رهن وقرىء ( فرهن ) بضم الهاء وسكونها وهو جمع رهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel is singled out because writing and witnesses may be unavailable; a pledge preserves property in their place, not because pledging is forbidden at home. The Prophet pledged his armor while not travelling.
rows.anchor: ليس الغرض تجويز الارتهان في السفر خاصة ولكن السفر لما كان مظنة لاعواز الكتب والإشهاد

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk restrict pledging to travel by the apparent wording and require possession; Mālik validates it by offer and acceptance without possession.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد والضحاك انهما لم يجوزاه الا في حال السفر أخذا بظاهر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some creditors trust a debtor because of their good opinion of him.
rows.anchor: فإن أمن بعض الدائنين بعض المديونين لحسن ظنه به

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads the passive ‘if the debtor is trusted,’ describing a person known for reliability, fulfillment, and independence from collateral.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( فإن أومن ) أي آمنه الناس ووصفوا المديون بالأمانة والوفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor should honor the creditor’s trust by repaying the entrusted debt; it is called trust because the creditor relied on him without collateral.
rows.anchor: حث المديون على أن يكون عند ظن الدائن به وامنه منه وائتمانه له وان يؤدي اليه الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase has alternative pronunciations; ʿĀṣim’s assimilation in ittaman is rejected because its yāʾ derives from hamza and remains hamza-like.
rows.anchor: وعن عاصم انه قرأ ( الذي اتمن ) بإدغام الياء في التاء قياسا على اتسر في الافتعال من اليسر وليس بصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘His heart is sinful’ can make the heart the subject of āthim or the topic with a fronted predicate; both mean the heart itself sins.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قلبه ﴾ رفع بآثم على الفاعلية كانه قيل فإنه يأثم قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the heart emphasizes that concealment begins inwardly; the heart is the body’s chief organ and root of its deeds, so the sin is grave, not merely a failure of speech.
rows.anchor: فلما كان إثما مقترفا بالقلب أسند اليه لأن إسناد الفعل إلى الجارحة التي يعمل بها أبلغ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās counts association, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest sins.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أكبر الكبائر الاشراك بالله لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading puts qalbahu in the accusative, like safiha nafsahu in 2:130.
rows.anchor: وشهادة الزور وكتمان الشهادة وقرىء ( قلبه ) بالنصب كقوله

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads athima qalbuhu, meaning he made his heart sinful.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( أثم قلبه ) أي جعله إثما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be steadfast in religion and obligations; outlast God’s enemies in jihad by enduring hardship, this specialized patience being singled out after patience generally.
rows.anchor: اصبروا على الدين وتكاليفه ﴿ وصابروا ﴾ أعداء الله في الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribāṭ means staying at frontier posts with horses ready for a raid, as in 8:60.
rows.anchor: وأقيموا في الثغور رابطين خيلكم فيها مترصدين مستعدين للغزو قال الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report equates a day and night guarding the frontier with a month of fasting and prayer, uninterrupted except for need.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 247 ( من رابط يوما وليلة في سبيل الله كان كعدل صيام شهر وقيامه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises safety on the bridge over Hell for every verse of Āl ʿImrān to its reciter.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم 248 ( من قرأ سورة آل عمران أعطى بكل آية منها امانا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: Another report says God and His angels bless whoever recites Āl ʿImrān on Friday until sunset.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام 249 ( من قرأ السورة التي يذكر فيها آل عمران يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Test orphans’ judgment, dispositions, and property management before puberty; once sound judgment is clear, transfer their assets at puberty without delay.
rows.anchor: واختبروا عقولهم وذوقوا احوالهم ومعرفتهم بالتصرف قبل البلوغ حتى اذا تبينتم منهم رشدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Reaching marriage’ means puberty, marked by a wet dream, when one is ready for procreation; ānastum means ascertain, by extension from perceiving.
rows.anchor: وبلوغ النكاح ان يحتلم لأنه يصلح للنكاح عنده ولطلب ما هو مقصود به

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and companions test by entrusting property for a youth to manage; sound judgment is knowing how to handle transactions.
rows.anchor: فالابتلاء عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه ان يدفع اليه ما يتصرف فيه حتى يستبين حاله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines sound judgment as mental uprightness and protecting property.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الصلاح في العقل والحفظ للمال

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī observe transactions and signs of piety; they define sound judgment as religious rectitude because sin damages property.
rows.anchor: وعند مالك والشافعي الابتلاء أن يتتبع أحواله وتصرفه في الأخذ والاعطاء

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: If judgment is absent at puberty, Abū Ḥanīfa waits until age twenty-five: puberty at eighteen plus seven years of human change, then releases the property even without prudence.
rows.anchor: ينتظر إلى خمس وعشرين سنة لأن مدة بلوغ الذكر عنده بالسن ثماني عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: أصحابه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa’s companions never release the property unless sound judgment appears.
rows.anchor: وعند أصحابه لا يدفع اليه ابدا الا بإيناس الرشد

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: The cited report says to command children to pray at seven, supporting the seven-year period.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 257 ( مروهم بالصلاة لسبع )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite wording permits any demonstrated aptitude in commerce rather than requiring complete maturity.
rows.anchor: معناه نوعا من الرشد وهو الرشد في التصرف والتجارة أو طرفا من الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The until-clause sets the limit of testing; puberty begins a conditional sequence, and transfer follows only if sound judgment is observed.
rows.anchor: جعل غاية للإبتلاء وهي ( حتى ) التي تقع بعدها الجمل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads aḥsastum (‘perceived’) instead of ānastum.
rows.anchor: وقرا ابن مسعود ( فإن أحسيتم ) بمعنى أحسستم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for sound judgment is read with fatḥa or ḍamma on both syllables.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( رشدا ) بفتحتين ( ورشدا ) بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition targets guardians spending lavishly or hastening to consume assets before orphans grow up and reclaim them.
rows.anchor: مسرفين ومبادرين كبرهم أو لإسرافكم ومبادرتكم كبرهم تفرطون في إنفاقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian abstains; a poor guardian may take a measured allowance as wages or a loan, a matter of disagreement.
rows.anchor: والفقير ياكل قوتا مقدرا محتاطا في تقديره على وجه الاجرة أو استقراضا على ما في ذلك من الاختلاف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked about an orphan in his care, the Prophet permits customary food without accumulating wealth or protecting one’s property with the orphan’s, and says discipline as one would a child.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 258 ان رجلا قال له ان في حجري يتيما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās allows drinking an orphan’s camel milk if the guardian tends, waters, and treats the animals without harming offspring or overmilking.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن ولي اليتيم قال له أفأشرب من لبن ابله قال ان كنت تبغي ضالتها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report allows eating proportionately while working with the orphans and wearing only modest clothing.
rows.anchor: وعنه يضرب بيده مع أيديهم فليأكل بالمعروف ولا يلبس عمامة فما فوقها

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm forbids linen and fine clothes, allowing only food that satisfies hunger and clothing that covers nakedness.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم لا يلبس الكتان والحلل ولكن ما سد الجوعة ووارى العورة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb says the guardian eats sparingly, like an animal grazing, and treats himself as a hired worker taking only what is necessary.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب يتقرم تقرم البهيمة وينزل نفسه منزلة الأجير فيما لا بد منه

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī allows food in proportion to work; another report compares it to carrion, permitting only necessity with repayment later.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي يأكل من ماله بقدر ما يعين فيه وعنه كالميتة يتناول عند الضرورة ويقضي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says take a loan from the orphan’s property and repay when able.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد يستسلف فاذا أيسر أدى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr allows surplus milk, riding, covering clothes, and food within limits; repay if able, and an insolvent guardian is excused.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير إن شاء شرب فضل اللبن وركب الظهر ولبس ما يستره من الثياب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar compares public funds to an orphan’s property: abstain if wealthy, eat moderately if poor, and repay when able; istaʿiff implies added abstention.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه إني انزلت نفسي من مال الله منزلة والي اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witness transfer to establish receipt, discharge the guardian’s liability, and prevent later dispute or denial.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأشهدوا عليهم ﴾ بانهم تسلموها وقبضوها وبرئت عنها ذممكم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Without witnesses, Abū Ḥanīfa’s school accepts the guardian’s claim on oath; Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī require proof, making witnesses protection from suspicion and liability.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى انه اذا لم يشهد فادعى عليه صدق مع اليمين عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God suffices as witness to delivery and receipt, or as accountant; guardians should be honest and avoid falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي كافيا في الشهادة عليكم بالدفع والقبض أو محاسبا فعليكم بالتصادق واياكم والتكاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They said it is only worldly life’ can coordinate with ‘they would return’ or ‘they are liars’; the latter means they lie in everything and made this claim.
rows.anchor: كما كانوا يقولون قبل معاينة القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that life is only worldly is itself evidence they are liars.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين قالوا : إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا . وكفى به دليلا على كذبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing before the Lord is a metaphor for detention and rebuke like a guilty servant before his master; alternatives say they encounter His recompense or recognize Him fully.
rows.anchor: مجاز على الحبس للتوبيخ والسؤال ، كما يوقف العبد الجاني بين يدي سيده ليعاتبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Is this not the truth?’ answers an imagined question about God’s words and rebukes their denial of resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعيير من الله تعالى لهم على التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They taste punishment because they disbelieved in meeting God and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: بكفركم بلقاء الله ببلوغ الآخرة وما يتصل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā ends their denial, not their loss, which has no endpoint; denial continued until the Hour brought regret.
rows.anchor: غاية لكذبوا لا لخسر ، لأن خسرانهم لا غاية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is the start of the afterlife and its preliminaries, so it counts as part of the Hour.
rows.anchor: لما كان الموت وقوعا في أحوال الآخرة ومقدماتها جعل من جنس الساعة وسمي باسمها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever dies has begun his resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 373 ) ( من مات فقد قامت قيامته )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Hour follows death so quickly that it is like an unexpected strike.
rows.anchor: أو جعل مجيء الساعة بعد الموت لسرعته كالوقاع بغير فترة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly, either as a circumstantial adverb or an absolute verbal noun emphasizing surprise.
rows.anchor: { بغتة } فجأة وانتصابها على الحال بمعنى باغتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We neglected it’ refers to worldly life, understood from context, or to the Hour and belief in it, as in ‘I neglected God’s side.’
rows.anchor: الضمير للحياة الدنيا ، جيء بضميرها وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لكونها معلومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sins are carried on their backs as burdens are customarily carried there; the wording compares this with deeds of the hands in 42:30.
rows.anchor: لأنه اعتيد حمل الأثقال على الظهور ، كما ألف الكسب بالأيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Evil is what they bear’ means their burden is a wretched thing, like the construction in 7:177.
rows.anchor: بئس شيئا يزرون وزرهم ، كقوله { ساء مثلا القوم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people disputed monotheism; ‘God guided me’ means He guided him to affirm divine oneness.
rows.anchor: وكانوا حاجوه في توحيد الله ونفي الشركاء عنه منكرين لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They warned idols could harm Abraham. He fears them only if God wills harm, perhaps for a sin or by enabling the idols; God knows all.
rows.anchor: وقد خوفوه أن معبوداتهم تصيبه بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal asks them to distinguish sound from false and the capable from the powerless.
rows.anchor: فتميزوا بين الصحيح والفاسد والقادر والعاجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham contrasts fearing powerless idols with their failure to fear associating God with beings unsupported by proof.
rows.anchor: وما لكم تنكرون علي الأمن في موضع الأمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He avoids asking which of himself and the polytheists is safer, to avoid praising himself, and instead asks which group is more entitled to security.
rows.anchor: احترازا من تزكيته نفسه ، فعدل عنه إلى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do not mix faith with wrongdoing avoid sins that make them impious; interpreting wrongdoing as unbelief conflicts with ‘mix.’
rows.anchor: أي لم يخلطوا إيمانهم بمعصية تفسقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ points to Abraham’s whole argument, from the setting of night to his people being guided; God guided and enabled him to make it.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى جميع ما احتج به إبراهيم عليه السلام على قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading gives tanwīn to darajāt; raising ranks means advancement in knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: يعني في العلم والحكمة . وقرىء بالتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘his descendants’ may refer to Noah or Abraham; David coordinates with Noah, and ‘some of their fathers’ is accusative with kullā, meaning some ancestors were favored.
rows.anchor: الضمير لنوح أو لإبراهيم . و { داوود } عطف على نوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even exalted prophets would have deeds nullified by association, as stated in 39:65.
rows.anchor: مع فضلهم وتقدمهم وما رفع لهم من الدرجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘These’ means Meccans; if they reject scripture, prophethood, and wisdom, the entrusted community can be the named prophets and their followers.
rows.anchor: { هاؤلاء } يعني أهل مكة { قوما } هم الأنبياء المذكورون ومن تابعهم

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Other identifications are the Prophet’s companions and believers, all believers among humanity, or angels; the Anṣār claimed the reference for themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هم أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكل من آمن به

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the entrusted community as the Persians.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : هم الفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entrusting means enabling them to believe, fulfill the scripture’s rights, and preserve it; bi-hā attaches to kāfirīn and repetition of negation emphasizes they will not reject it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى توكيلهم بها : أنهم وفقوا للإيمان بها والقيام بحقوقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following their guidance is limited to faith in God and fundamentals, not differing or abrogated laws; the hāʾ in iqtidah marks pause and remains in the codex.
rows.anchor: { فبهداهم اقتده } فاختص هداهم بالاقتداء ، ولا تقتد إلا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿālaw began as an invitation spoken from a high place to those below, then broadened to a general invitation.
rows.anchor: من الخاص الذي صار عاما ، وأصله أن يقوله من كان في مكان عال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā ḥarrama is the object of recitation or an indirect question; anlā is explanatory and lā prohibitive.
rows.anchor: منصوب بفعل التلاوة ، أي أتل الذي حرمه ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not treat anlā as an accusative particle with ‘do not associate’ as an apposition; prohibitions coordinate with the ensuing imperatives.
rows.anchor: نواهي لانعطاف الأوامر عليها ، وهي قوله : { وبالوالدين إحسانا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the fatha reading of ‘and this is My path,’ supply a purpose lām: follow it because it is straight; the kasra reading gives the same cause, supported by 72:18.
rows.anchor: قلت : أجعل قوله : { وأن هاذا صراطي مستقيما } ( الأنعام : 153 ) علة للاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands and prohibitions share the opening ruling; it prohibits their opposites, including mistreating parents, short measures, unjust speech, and breaking the covenant.
rows.anchor: علم أن التحريم راجع إلى أضدادها ، وهي الإساءة إلى الوالدين ، وبخس الكيل والميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min imlāq means because of poverty or fear of poverty, as in 17:31.
rows.anchor: من أجل فقر ومن خشيته ، كقوله تعالى : { خشية إملاق } ( الإسراء : 31 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What is apparent and hidden’ parallels the outward and inward sin mentioned in 6:120.
rows.anchor: مثل قوله : { ظاهر الإثم وباطنه } ( الأنعام : 120 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Killing ‘except by right’ includes retaliation, execution for apostasy, and stoning.
rows.anchor: كالقصاص ، والقتل على الردة ، والرجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best handling of an orphan’s property is to preserve and grow it until maturity, then hand it over.
rows.anchor: إلا بالخصلة التي هي أحسن ما يفعل بمال اليتيم ، وهي حفظه وتثميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By fairness means accurate equality; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity.
rows.anchor: السوية والعدل ؛ { لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها } إلا ما يسعها ولا تعجز عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The capacity qualification follows exact measurement because staying precisely at the just limit may be difficult; one must reach ability and is excused beyond it.
rows.anchor: لأن مراعاة الحد من القسط الذي لا زيادة فيه ولا نقصان مما يجري فيه الحرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speak justly in testimony about relatives without adding or withholding, as 4:135 likewise commands.
rows.anchor: ولو كان المقول له أو عليه في شهادة أو غيرها من أهل قرابة القاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A light-an reading has an omitted pronoun of the matter; al-Aʿmash reads ‘this is My path,’ while the ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy codices read ‘this is your Lord’s path.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما ) بتخفيف ( أن ) وأصله : وأنه هذا صراطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divergent paths are Judaism, Christianity, Magianism, innovations, and misguidance; they divide people away from Islam.
rows.anchor: الطرق المختلفة في الدين ، من اليهودية والنصرانية ، والمجوسية ، وسائر البدع والضلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading assimilates the tāʾ in fatafarraqa.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فتفرق ) بإدغام التاء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet drew one line as right guidance and side lines each with a devil calling to it, then recited the verse.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو وائل عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 383 ) أنه خط خطا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these commandments are established and never abrogated in any scripture.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Another report calls them scripture’s foundation: those who follow enter Paradise and those who abandon them enter Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنهن أم الكتاب ، من عمل بهن دخل الجنة ، ومن تركهن دخل النار

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār swears these commandments were the first thing in the Torah.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب الأحبار : والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذه الآيات لأول شيء في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then We gave Moses the Book’ coordinates with ‘He enjoined you’; the command is ancient and was entrusted to each community through its prophet.
rows.anchor: هذه التوصية قديمة ، لم تزل توصاها كل أمة على لسان نبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A declarative reading of ‘Have you believed him?’ rebukes the magicians; an interrogative reading expresses denial and incredulity.
rows.anchor: ءامنتم به } على الإخبار ، أي فعلتم هذا الفعل الشنيع ، توبيخا لهم وتقريعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh alleges that Moses and the magicians conspired in Egypt before the exodus to expel the Copts and settle Israelites, as propaganda against their conversion.
rows.anchor: إن صنعكم هذا لحيلة احتلتموها أنتم وموسى في مصر قبل أن تخرجوا إلى هذه الصحراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses asked the chief magician whether he would believe if defeated; the magician promised to believe if his unbeatable magic lost, and Pharaoh heard.
rows.anchor: وروي أن موسى عليه السلام قال للساحر الأكبر : أتؤمن بي إن غلبتك ؟ قال : لآتين بسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s general threat is specified by cutting and crucifixion; readings lighten the lām in both verbs.
rows.anchor: وعيد أجمله ثم فصله بقوله : { لاقطعن } وقرىء : ( لأقطعن ) بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting ‘from opposite sides’ means taking a limb from each opposing side of the body.
rows.anchor: { من خلاف } من كل شق طرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said Pharaoh was the first to cut and crucify people crosswise.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أول من قطع من خلاف وصلب لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidden months were a respite during which treaty-breakers could travel safely; afterward fight those who broke the pact and sided against Muslims.
rows.anchor: { الاشهر الحرم } التي أبيح فيها للناكثين أن يسيحوا { فاقتلوا المشركين } يعني الذين نقضوكم وظاهروا عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may be killed anywhere, captured and imprisoned, and prevented from moving through the land.
rows.anchor: { حيث وجدتموهم } من حل أو حرم { وخذوهم } وأسروهم . والأخيذ : الأسير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains besieging them as preventing them from reaching the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : حصرهم أن يحال بينهم وبين المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every marṣad is a pass to watch; the adverbial construction parallels waiting on God’s straight path in 7:16.
rows.anchor: { كل مرصد } كل ممر مجتاز ترصدونهم به ، وانتصابه على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After capture and confinement, release them; alternatively, stop pursuing them, as in the cited poem about leaving the road open.
rows.anchor: { فخلوا سبيلهم } فأطلقوا عنهم بعد الأسر والحصر . أو فكفوا عنهم ولا تتعرضوا لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses this as allowing them to go and enter the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : دعوهم وإتيان المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives them for their former unbelief and betrayal.
rows.anchor: يغفر لهم ما سلف من الكفر والغدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides from heaven and earth, pouring out His favors and widening His mercy.
rows.anchor: أي يرزقكم منهما جميعا ، لم يقتصر برزقكم على جهة واحدة ليفيض عليكم نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Who owns hearing and sight?’ asks who creates and fashions them remarkably, or who protects these delicate organs from many hazards.
rows.anchor: من يستطيع خلقهما وتسويتهما على الحد الذي سويا عليه من الفطرة العجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Managing affairs means directing the whole world, stated generally after specific examples.
rows.anchor: ومن يلي تدبير أمر العالم كله ، جاء بالعموم بعد الخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Will you not fear?’ means protect yourselves from punishment for your misguidance.
rows.anchor: أفلا تقون أنفسكم ولا تحذرون عليها عقابه فيما أنتم بصدده من الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one with these powers is the true Lord; truth and error have no middle ground, so leaving truth means entering misguidance, shirk, and misery.
rows.anchor: الثابت ربوبيته ثباتا لا ريب فيه لمن حقق النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘How are you turned away?’ asks how they turn from truth to error and monotheism to association.
rows.anchor: عن الحق إلى الضلال ، وعن التوحيد إلى الشرك ، وعن السعادة إلى الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The settled word may mean the extreme disbelievers will not believe, which God knew; alternatively it is His decree they are forsaken or promise of punishment because they disbelieve.
rows.anchor: و { أنهم لا يؤمنون } بدل من الكلمة أي حق عليهم انتفاء الإيمان ، وعلم الله منهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer with clear proof from his Lord is far above seekers of worldly life; this refers to converts from Judaism such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām.
rows.anchor: وأراد بهم من آمن من اليهود كعبد الله بن سلام وغيره ، كان على بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof is a rational demonstration Islam is true; the Qur’an follows it as confirming witness from God or a witness from the believer who has the proof.
rows.anchor: أي شاهد يشهد بصحته ، وهو القرآن { منه } من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah preceded the Qur’an and follows the proof as an exemplar in religion and a mercy for its recipients.
rows.anchor: أي : ويتلو ذلك البرهان أيضا من قبل القرآن كتاب موسى . وقرىء : ( كتاب موسى ) بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those on the proof believe the Qur’an; rejecting factions are Meccans and allies of the Prophet’s opponents, whose destination is the Fire.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل مكة ومن ضامهم من المتحزبين على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meriyah is read with kasra or ḍamma; both mean doubt.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( مرية ) بالضم وهما الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘From it’ may refer to the Qur’an or the promised punishment.
rows.anchor: { منه } من القرآن أو من الموعد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ʿashiyyan as a diminutive; Ibn Jinnī reports a short form with ḍamma and says they were blinded by weeping.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ( عشيا ) على تصغير عشى يقال : لقيته عشيا وعشيانا ، وأصيلا وأصيلانا ورواه ابن جني

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: When a woman cried before Shurayḥ, al-Shaʿbī noted Joseph’s brothers also wept despite being wrongdoers; judgment follows the prescribed Sunnah.
rows.anchor: فقال له الشعبي : يا أبا أمية ، أما تراها تبكي ؟ فقال : قد جاء إخوة يوسف يبكون وهم ظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jacob panicked at their voices, asked whether the flock was harmed, then asked why they had come and where Joseph was.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما سمع صوتهم فزع وقال : ما لكم يا بني ؟ هل أصابكم في غنمكم شيء ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nastabiqu means they raced; iftiʿāl and tafāʿul may share meaning, and they could race by running or archery.
rows.anchor: أي نتسابق ، والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كالانتضال والتناضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say Jacob will not believe even if they are truthful because of his intense love for Joseph and distrust of them.
rows.anchor: ولو كنا عندك من أهل الصدق والثقة ، لشدة محبتك ليوسف ، فكيف وأنت سيء الظن بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dam kadhib means false blood, either a noun describing it or source-word hyperbole as though blood itself were falsehood.
rows.anchor: {بدم كذب } ذي كذب . أو وصف بالمصدر مبالغة ، كأنه نفس الكذب وعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has kadhiban in the accusative as a circumstantial expression or causal object.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( كذبا ) نصبا على الحال ، بمعنى جاءوا به كاذبين

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reads kadb with dāl, meaning cloudy or, alternatively, fresh; Ibn Jinnī derives it from white spots on young people’s nails.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عائشة رضي الله عنها : كدب ، بالدال غير المعجمة ، أي كدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the brothers slaughtered a lamb and smeared its blood on the shirt, forgetting to tear it.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم ذبحوا سخلة ولطخوه بدمها ، وزل عنهم أن يمزقوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asked for the shirt, put it on his face, and cried until blood stained him; he remarked that no wolf was more patient, eating a son without tearing the shirt.
rows.anchor: وروي أن يعقوب لما سمع بخبر يوسف صاح بأعلى صوته وقال : أين القميص ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt had three signs: it exposed the brothers’ lie, restored Jacob’s sight on his face, and proved Joseph innocent when torn from behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان في قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات : كان دليلا ليعقوب على كذبهم ، وألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlā qamīṣihi is an adverbial accusative meaning ‘above his shirt’; a genitive’s circumstantial phrase cannot precede it.
rows.anchor: محله النصب على الظرف ، كأنه قيل : وجاءوا فوق قميصه بدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwalat means made easy, from a root suggesting slackness; Jacob inferred the deed from known envy and the intact shirt, or learned by revelation.
rows.anchor: { سولت } سهلت من السول وهو الاسترخاء ، أي : سهلت { لكم أنفسكم أمرا } عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ṣabrun jamīl may be a predicate or topic; Ubayy reads fa-ṣabran jamīlan.
rows.anchor: { فصبر جميل } خبر أو مبتدأ لكونه موصوفا أي فأمري صبر جميل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report defines beautiful patience as patience without complaint to people, consistent with Jacob’s words in 12:86.
rows.anchor: والصبر الجميل جاء في الحديث المرفوع . ( 540 ) ( أنه الذي لا شكوى فيه إلى الخلق )

rows.speaker: وقيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Jacob would not meet them with a gloomy face but treat them as before.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لا أعايشكم على كآبة الوجه ، بل أكون لكم كما كنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jacob’s brows fell over his eyes from grief; when God asked if he complained of Him, Jacob called it his fault and asked forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليه : يا يعقوب أتشكوني ؟ قال : يا رب . خطيئة فاغفرها لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘God is the one whose help is sought’ means Jacob asks God to help endure Joseph’s loss and the brothers’ account.
rows.anchor: أي أستعينه { على } احتمال { ما تصفون } من هلاك يوسف والصبر على الرزء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the subject and ‘who created’ its predicate; min al-thamarāt clarifies provision or is the object of ‘brought forth,’ with rizqan circumstantial or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: { الله } مبتدأ ، و { الذى خلق } خبره ، و { من الثمرات } بيان للرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By His command means by His word ‘Be’; dāʾibayn describes the sun and moon constantly travelling, shining, dispelling darkness, and benefiting earth, bodies, and plants.
rows.anchor: { بأمره } بقوله كن { دائبين } يدأبان في سيرهما وإنارتهما ودرئهما الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon alternate for livelihood and rest.
rows.anchor: { وسخر لكم الشمس والقمر } يتعاقبان خلفة لمعاشكم وسباتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive: God granted some of everything requested, with human interests in view.
rows.anchor: من للتبعيض ، أي آتاكم بعض جميع ما سألتموه ، نظرا في مصالحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With tanwīn on kull, mā may be negative, yielding gifts unsought; alternatively it is relative and means necessities, as if requested by need.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( من كل ) بالتنوين ، وما سألتموه نفي ومحله النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You cannot encompass or count God’s blessings; only God can know them in detail.
rows.anchor: لا تحصروها ولا تطيقوا عدها وبلوغ آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans wrong blessings through ingratitude; alternatively, they complain in hardship and hoard in prosperity. ‘Human’ refers to the species.
rows.anchor: { لظلوم } يظلم النعمة بإغفال شكرها { كفار } شديد الكفران لها . وقيل ظلوم في الشدة يشكو

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī identifies those whose efforts were lost as monks, compared with those who toil in 88:3.
rows.anchor: ضل سعيهم } ضاع وبطل وهم الرهبان . عن علي رضي الله عنه ، كقوله : { عاملة ناصبة }

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says they are the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Asked by Ibn al-Kawwāʾ who they were, ʿAlī said some were the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : أن ابن الكوا سأله عنهم ؟ فقال : منهم أهل حروراء

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports people bringing deeds they thought immense as Tihāma’s mountains, yet weighing nothing.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري : يأتي ناس بأعمال يوم القيامة هي عندهم في العظم كجبال تهامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigns them no weight or worth; alternatively no scales are erected for them, because scales are reserved for monotheists with good and bad deeds.
rows.anchor: فنزدري بهم ولا يكون لهم عندنا وزن ومقدار . وقيل : لا يقام لهم ميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the verb in third-person masculine: fa-lā yuqīmu.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فلا يقيم ) ، بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those whose efforts were lost’ may be nominative as an answer, accusative as censure, or genitive as apposition.
rows.anchor: الأوجه أن يكون في محل الرفع ، على : هم الذين ضل سعيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannam is an appositional clarification of ‘their recompense.’
rows.anchor: { جهنم } عطف بيان لقوله : { جزآؤهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and their wonders were not made for play like tyrants’ ornamented roofs and floors; they serve religious benefit, divine wisdom, reflection, proof, and countless practical uses.
rows.anchor: وما سوينا هذا السقف المرفوع وهذا المهاد الموضوع وما بينهما من أصناف الخلائق مشحونة بضروب البدائع والعجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom rules out amusement in God’s actions, though He could choose it, since He has power over everything.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أن السبب في ترك اتخاذ اللهو واللعب وانتفائه عن أفعالي : هو أن الحكمة صارفة عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘From Us’ means from God’s power, as in 28:57; some say lahw means offspring in Yemeni usage or wife, and ‘from Us’ means angels, rejecting Christ’s and Ezra’s sonship.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { لاتخذناه من لدنا } ، كقوله : { رزقا من لدنا } ( القصص : 57 ) أي من جهة قدرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal rejects amusement and exalts God above it: wisdom and self-sufficiency lead Him to overcome play with seriousness and defeat falsehood with truth.
rows.anchor: {بل } إضراب عن اتخاذ اللهو واللعب ، وتنزيه منه لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Casting and crushing are metaphors for annihilating falsehood, pictured as a hard stone crushing a soft, hollow object.
rows.anchor: واستعار لذلك القذف والدمغ ، تصويرا لإبطاله وإهداره ومحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accusative reading of fa-yadmagh is judged weak, like the cited poetic subjunctive construction.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فيدمغه ) بالنصب ، وهو في ضعف قوله : سأترك منزلي لبني تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measure may be complete, deficient, or excessive: full measure is required and shortchanging forbidden; silence about excess implies it is good but not required.
rows.anchor: الكيل على ثلاثة أضرب : واف ، وطفيف ، وزائد . فأمر بالواجب الذي هو الإيفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisṭās is read with ḍamma or kasra and means a balance; qirsṭūn is another form, possibly from the root of justice or quadriliteral, and is said to mean justice in Greek.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( بالقسطاس ) مضمونا ومكسورا وهو الميزان وقيل : القرسطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakhs means reducing someone’s due; do not diminish established rights or unlawfully seize or use another’s property.
rows.anchor: يقال : بخسته حقه ، إذا نقصته إياه . ومنه قيل للمكس : البخس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAthā has variant forms and covers highway robbery, raiding, and crop destruction, which the corrupt people practiced and were forbidden.
rows.anchor: يقال : عثا في الأرض وعثى وعاث ، وذلك نحو قطع الطريق ، والغارة ، وإهلاك الزروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jibilla has readings with different patterns but the same meaning, natural constitution; dhawū al-jibilla means original people.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( الجبلة ) ، بوزن الأبلة . والجبلة ، بوزن الخلقة
